headline: Kraków’s Terrorism Label Is Not a Motive Finding
deck: The prime minister’s label and a minister’s ideological assessment frame the attack; neither establishes why it happened.
body: Poland began two days of national mourning after a 24-year-old man drove into Kraków’s Main Square and opened fire, killing six people before police shot and wounded him. [E1]
AP reported 15 people wounded, while Euronews reported 16 injured; neither report explains the difference. [E1][E8]
The dead were four women and two men; authorities said at least three of the women were Polish and one victim was a U.K. citizen. [E2]
The mourning period began at midnight on Sunday, with national flags flown at half-mast. [E3]
Prime Minister Donald Tusk named senior constable Jakub Kulik and senior constable Artur Morański as the officers who detained the attacker, calling them “true heroes.” [E4]
Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the attacker held “very radical” and “ultranationalistic” views and that everything indicated he had been fascinated by far-right ideologies. [E5]
Police said three bodies found at the attacker’s home were his sister, mother and father, and that they likely died from gunshot wounds. [E6][E7]
Tusk separately called the shooting an act of terrorism. [E8]

The public framing therefore has distinct parts: officers stopped the attacker, the prime minister applied an official label to the attack, and the interior minister offered an assessment of the attacker’s views. That chain explains how the state can mark the event and mourn its victims without turning an assessment of ideology into a demonstrated cause of every death in the sequence. [E4][E5][E6][E7][E8]

**The desk's reading.** Poland has an official terrorism label and an official assessment of far-right fascination, but neither is itself a motive finding. The strongest competing reading is that the violence and the minister’s assessment already explain the attack. But the reported facts do not connect that assessment causally to the shooting or to the deaths at the attacker’s home, so the narrower distinction is the one the evidence can carry.

**The next test.** The first police or prosecutor account released after the two-day mourning period should state whether it links the attacker’s ideology to the shooting and the deaths at home. A documented causal link would support the competing reading; an account that limits the finding to an assessment of views, or treats the deaths as a separate sequence, would support the desk’s reading. [E3]
